# Looks Good to AI Formerly AI Code Review Triage **AI writes code faster than you can read it. Stop reading harder and review differently.** An [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io) that reviews AI-written pull requests by splitting "reading the code" into three separate jobs.
Runs in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, Kiro, Amp, Junie and Zed, and loads as plain context in Aider. 🇬🇧 · 🇨🇳 · 🇯🇵 · 🇰🇷 · 🇪🇸 · 🇧🇷 · 🇫🇷 [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent_Skills-compatible-1b1b19?style=flat-square)](https://agentskills.io/specification) [![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-plugin-d97757?style=flat-square)](#claude-code-plugin) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-1b1b19?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-1b1b19?style=flat-square)](CHANGELOG.md) [![CI](https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai/actions/workflows/ci.yml) Quick start · The idea · Install · Usage · Examples · How it works · Limits
--- ## The problem Agent-written PRs pile up faster than anyone can review them line by line. Reading harder doesn't help much either: the code is tidy on the surface, so the real problems hide well enough to survive a careful read. "Just merge and roll back if it breaks" works technically, but a human still answers for the incident. ## Quick start ```sh npx skills add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai ``` The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI asks which agents to set up. Add `-g` to install for your user instead of this project, and `-a ` to skip the question (`-a claude-code`, `-a codex`, `-a github-copilot`, `-a cursor`, …). Or use the agent's own installer: | Agent | Command | |---|---| | Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai` then `/plugin install looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai` | | Codex | `codex plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai` then `codex plugin add looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai` | | GitHub Copilot CLI | `copilot plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai` then `copilot plugin install looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai` | | Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai` | Then, in your agent: ```text Review this AI-generated PR before I merge it. ``` The skill loads on its own from a request like that. Most agents also take `/looks-good-to-ai` to call it by name; Codex uses `$looks-good-to-ai`. [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md) has the command for each agent. ## The idea "Reviewing code" has always bundled three different jobs. That worked when code arrived slowly. At agent speed, each job needs its own process: ```mermaid flowchart LR PR([AI-written PR]) --> T{Step 0
Triage
risk tier} T --> B["**1 · Catch bugs**
fresh-context sub-agent
+ tests / repro"] B --> C["**2 · Align context**
orders of magnitude
history & neighbors
requirement match"] C --> S["**3 · Own the sign-off**
explain · detect · undo
scoped approval"] S --> R([Review report]) ``` | Job | Question | Who does it best | |---|---|---| | **Catch bugs** | Is the code wrong? | Machines, with an *independent* second pass | | **Align context** | Is this the right change for this product, today? | A human, checking angles the diff can't show | | **Own the sign-off** | Will I put my name on this? | The approver, with an explicit scope | Low-risk PRs only run Step 1. Medium-risk PRs run Steps 1 and 2. High-risk PRs (production behavior, data, security, money) run all three. ### What it catches that line-by-line review misses > A PR changes `SESSION_TIMEOUT = 30` to `30000` and drops one line of unit conversion. Tests pass. The code is clean. A line-by-line reader approves it in 30 seconds. > > - **Step 1** has a fresh-context sub-agent add a boundary test. Result: sessions now expire after **30 seconds**. > - **Step 2** checks history and callers. The same change was reverted once before, the mobile client hard-codes the old value, and the request was only for "remember me" users while the diff changes everyone. > - **Step 3** blocks the approval. Nobody can explain what the PR actually does. > > Full run: [examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md](examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md) ## Install The skill is the folder [`skills/looks-good-to-ai/`](skills/looks-good-to-ai). Every agent below loads it unchanged; only the folder differs. [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md) has the full table with every folder each agent reads, the way each agent calls a skill, and a link to each agent's own documentation. | Agent | skills CLI | Or copy the folder to (user · project) | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `-a claude-code` | `~/.claude/skills/` · `.claude/skills/` | | Codex | `-a codex` | `~/.agents/skills/` · `.agents/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `-a github-copilot` | `~/.copilot/skills/` · `.github/skills/` | | Cursor | `-a cursor` | `~/.cursor/skills/` · `.cursor/skills/` | | Gemini CLI | `-a gemini-cli` | `~/.gemini/skills/` · `.gemini/skills/` | | Antigravity | `-a antigravity` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` · `.agents/skills/` | | OpenCode | `-a opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/` · `.opencode/skills/` | | Windsurf | `-a windsurf` | `~/.config/devin/skills/` · `.devin/skills/` | | Cline | copy by hand ([why](docs/agents.md#cline)) | `~/.cline/skills/` · `.cline/skills/` | | Roo Code | `-a roo` | `~/.roo/skills/` · `.roo/skills/` | | Kiro | `-a kiro-cli` | `~/.kiro/skills/` · `.kiro/skills/` | | Amp | `-a amp` | `~/.config/agents/skills/` · `.agents/skills/` | | Junie | `-a junie` | `~/.junie/skills/` · `.junie/skills/` | | Zed | `-a zed` | `~/.agents/skills/` · `.agents/skills/` | | Aider | — | `read:` in `.aider.conf.yml` ([how](docs/agents.md#aider)) | | Continue | — | Unverified; load as a rule ([how](docs/agents.md#continue)) |
With git, no CLI
Clone the repository once and copy the skill folder into the agent's folder from the table, so that `SKILL.md` ends up at `/looks-good-to-ai/SKILL.md`: ```sh git clone https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai.git cp -r looks-good-to-ai/skills/looks-good-to-ai ~/.claude/skills/ ``` Swap `~/.claude/skills/` for any other folder in the table. For a project install, commit the copied folder so your team gets it too.
On every pull request (GitHub Actions)
A reusable workflow runs the skill on each pull request and posts the report as a comment. Setup takes three steps: [docs/github-action.md](docs/github-action.md).
Claude Code plugin
Inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai /plugin install looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai ```
## Usage Ask your agent something like: - *"Review this AI-generated PR before I merge it."* - *"Can this diff be merged? Codex wrote it."* - *"I'm about to approve #123. What should I verify first?"* - *"We have too many agent PRs to read line by line. Triage this one."* You get a report like this (from the invented timeout example): ```markdown ## Extend session lifetime for "remember me" · Risk: High ### 1. Bugs (independent fresh-context review) - [CONFIRMED] auth/session.py:3 — unit conversion dropped; sessions expire after 30 s. Repro: test_session_expires_after_timeout ### 2. Context - Magnitudes: SESSION_TIMEOUT 30 → 30000 (comment says min, code treats as ms) — suspicious - History / neighbors: reverted once before (a1b2c3d); mobile/src/config.ts hard-codes 30 min - Requirement match: asked for remember-me users only; diff changes everyone ### 3. Sign-off - Detection: login-rate and 401-rate alerts · Rollback: config revert - Recommendation: request changes - Verification scope: verified units and callers; did not load-test Reviewed with [Looks Good to AI](https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai) ``` The last line credits the skill when you paste the report into a PR. Ask the agent to leave it out if you don't want it.
More prompts, from the skill's evals
```text Here's the diff for PR #482. Cursor wrote it to raise our retry count from 3 to 10 on the payments client. Tests pass. Can I approve it? ``` ```text Copilot opened a PR that only fixes typos in docs/ and the README. Do I need the full review process? ``` ```text I wrote this change with you in this session. Now review it before I merge. ```
## Examples Both walkthroughs are invented scenarios that follow one PR through every step. | Walkthrough | What goes wrong | What finds it | |---|---|---| | [Session timeout](examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md) | `30` → `30000` with the unit conversion dropped: sessions expire after 30 seconds, for every user. | A boundary test in Step 1; units, a past revert and a hard-coded mobile value in Step 2. | | [Pagination limit](examples/pagination-limit-walkthrough.md) | Page size `100` → `1000` against a provider that caps pages at 100: the export stops with 150 of 250 rows missing. | The provider contract in Step 2, and a standard-library Python reproduction you can run. | ## How it works - **[`SKILL.md`](skills/looks-good-to-ai/SKILL.md)** is what the agent reads: the risk tiers, the three steps, the commands for history and callers, and the report template. - **Step 1 needs a second, clean context.** The session that wrote the code can't review it independently. [`references/subagents.md`](skills/looks-good-to-ai/references/subagents.md) shows how each agent starts a fresh reviewer, and what to do in agents that have none. - **Step 2 needs a shell with `git`.** It runs `git log -S`, `git log --grep=revert` and `grep` to find history and callers the diff doesn't show. - **[`evals/evals.json`](evals/evals.json)** holds test prompts and what a good answer contains. CI checks that the skill's frontmatter follows the [Agent Skills spec](https://agentskills.io/specification) and that the pagination reproduction still runs.
Repository layout
```text looks-good-to-ai/ ├── skills/looks-good-to-ai/ the skill (this folder is what gets installed) │ ├── SKILL.md workflow, risk tiers, report template │ ├── references/subagents.md a fresh-context reviewer in each agent │ └── agents/openai.yaml display name for the Codex and ChatGPT apps ├── docs/ │ ├── agents.md install and use in each agent, with sources │ └── review-ai-generated-code.md questions and answers ├── examples/ two invented end-to-end walkthroughs ├── evals/evals.json test prompts and expected answers ├── scripts/check.py the checks CI runs ├── .claude-plugin/ plugin and marketplace manifests (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI) ├── gemini-extension.json Gemini CLI extension manifest └── .github/ CI, issue forms, PR template ```
## Limits - **It is a review process, not a scanner.** It decides what has to be true before you approve. Run linters, type checkers and security tools inside Step 1; this skill does not replace them. - **It can't guarantee a PR is safe.** The examples are invented teaching cases, not a measured detection rate. - **It is slower than a skim, on purpose.** A high-risk PR gets a sub-agent pass, tests, history searches and a written sign-off. Low-risk PRs skip most of it. - **Step 1 is only as independent as the reviewer you give it.** In agents without sub-agents, open a new session by hand. Questions such as "can it review Codex output?" and "why can passing tests miss incomplete exports?" are answered in [docs/review-ai-generated-code.md](docs/review-ai-generated-code.md). ## Works well with This skill organizes the review and decides what has to be true before you approve. It doesn't replace specialized checkers. Run them inside Step 1: - a correctness-focused review (for example Claude Code's built-in `/code-review`, or Copilot CLI's code-review agent) - security and performance checklists - over-engineering reviews ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first: it covers linking a working copy into your agent, the checks CI runs, and what a change to `SKILL.md` has to keep. - [Report a problem](https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) - [Add or fix an agent](https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai/issues/new?template=agent_support.yml) - [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## Acknowledgments The three-job framing was inspired by [a public talk](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1mRn66JERc/) on reviewing AI-written code. The multi-agent install layout follows [Anatomy](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) ---

Looks Good to AI finds four problems: a dropped unit conversion hidden in the diff, a past revert, a mobile client that hard-codes the old value, and a requirement mismatch. Read line by line, it logs every user out after 30 seconds; with the skill, it is blocked before merge" width="820">

---

The problem

Agent-written PRs pile up faster than anyone can review them line by line. Reading harder doesn't help much either: the code is tidy on the surface, so the real problems hide well enough to survive a careful read. "Just merge and roll back if it breaks" works technically, but a human still answers for the incident.

Quick start


npx skills add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai

The skills CLI asks which agents to set up. Add -g to install for your user instead of this project, and -a <agent> to skip the question (-a claude-code, -a codex, -a github-copilot, -a cursor, …).

Or use the agent's own installer:

| Agent | Command |

|---|---|

| Claude Code | /plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai then /plugin install looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai |

| Codex | codex plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai then codex plugin add looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai |

| GitHub Copilot CLI | copilot plugin marketplace add laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai then copilot plugin install looks-good-to-ai@looks-good-to-ai |

| Gemini CLI | gemini extensions install https://github.com/laulauraluo/looks-good-to-ai |

Then, in your agent:


Review this AI-generated PR before I merge it.

The skill loads on its own from a request like that. Most agents also take /looks-good-to-ai to call it by name; Codex uses $looks-good-to-ai. [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md) has the command for each agent.

The idea

"Reviewing code" has always bundled three different jobs. That worked when code arrived slowly. At agent speed, each job needs its own process:


flowchart LR

    PR([AI-written PR]) --> T{Step 0<br/>Triage<br/>risk tier}

    T --> B["**1 · Catch bugs**<br/>fresh-context sub-agent<br/>+ tests / repro"]

    B --> C["**2 · Align context**<br/>orders of magnitude<br/>history & neighbors<br/>requirement match"]

    C --> S["**3 · Own the sign-off**<br/>explain · detect · undo<br/>scoped approval"]

    S --> R([Review report])

| Job | Question | Who does it best |

|---|---|---|

| Catch bugs | Is the code wrong? | Machines, with an *independent* second pass |

| Align context | Is this the right change for this product, today? | A human, checking angles the diff can't show |

| Own the sign-off | Will I put my name on this? | The approver, with an explicit scope |

Low-risk PRs only run Step 1. Medium-risk PRs run Steps 1 and 2. High-risk PRs (production behavior, data, security, money) run all three.

What it catches that line-by-line review misses

> A PR changes SESSION_TIMEOUT = 30 to 30000 and drops one line of unit conversion. Tests pass. The code is clean. A line-by-line reader approves it in 30 seconds.

>

> - Step 1 has a fresh-context sub-agent add a boundary test. Result: sessions now expire after 30 seconds.

> - Step 2 checks history and callers. The same change was reverted once before, the mobile client hard-codes the old value, and the request was only for "remember me" users while the diff changes everyone.

> - Step 3 blocks the approval. Nobody can explain what the PR actually does.

>

> Full run: [examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md](examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md)

- [CONFIRMED] auth/session.py:3 — unit conversion dropped; sessions expire after 30 s. Repro: test_session_expires_after_timeout



### 2. Context

- Magnitudes: SESSION_TIMEOUT 30 → 30000 (comment says min, code treats as ms) — suspicious

- History / neighbors: reverted once before (a1b2c3d); mobile/src/config.ts hard-codes 30 min

- Requirement match: asked for remember-me users only; diff changes everyone

- Detection: login-rate and 401-rate alerts · Rollback: config revert

Examples

Both walkthroughs are invented scenarios that follow one PR through every step.

| Walkthrough | What goes wrong | What finds it |

|---|---|---|

| [Session timeout](examples/session-timeout-walkthrough.md) | 30 → 30000 with the unit conversion dropped: sessions expire after 30 seconds, for every user. | A boundary test in Step 1; units, a past revert and a hard-coded mobile value in Step 2. |

| [Pagination limit](examples/pagination-limit-walkthrough.md) | Page size 100 → 1000 against a provider that caps pages at 100: the export stops with 150 of 250 rows missing. | The provider contract in Step 2, and a standard-library Python reproduction you can run. |

How it works

  • [SKILL.md](skills/looks-good-to-ai/SKILL.md) is what the agent reads: the risk tiers, the three steps, the commands for history and callers, and the report template.
  • Step 1 needs a second, clean context. The session that wrote the code can't review it independently. [references/subagents.md](skills/looks-good-to-ai/references/subagents.md) shows how each agent starts a fresh reviewer, and what to do in agents that have none.
  • Step 2 needs a shell with git. It runs git log -S, git log --grep=revert and grep to find history and callers the diff doesn't show.
  • [evals/evals.json](evals/evals.json) holds test prompts and what a good answer contains. CI checks that the skill's frontmatter follows the Agent Skills spec and that the pagination reproduction still runs.
